# Little City

> A peaceful, hand-drawn city builder sandbox you play free in your browser (https://littlecity.io). No money, no goals, no tycoon: place a few blocks and watch a little town come alive.

Little City is a cozy town-building game drawn in ink and pencil, made by Derek Yao. It runs in any web browser on a computer, iPhone, iPad or Android phone, with no download, no account and no ads.

- It is not a tycoon or management game. There is no money, budget, zoning, traffic or score, and nothing can go wrong. Unlike Cities: Skylines, there is nothing to manage: it is closer to building a model town.
- You place simple pieces (house, tower, lighthouse, arch, dock, marble, pillar, mill, path, plaza, garden, fence, wall, and the Auto block), and the town works out what they become from where they are: a house beside a tall tower becomes a chapel, a house opening onto a square becomes a shop, four blocks stacked by the sea become a lighthouse. There are over 80 special buildings and events to discover.
- The town is alive: residents walk to work and you can follow the work from start to finish (flour from the windmill to the bakery, bread to the market stall and home), fishing boats, ships at the quay, washing on the lines, market days, weddings with a procession, beach days, picnics, snow days, harvest suppers, seasons, weather, and day and night.
- "Grow a town" grows a whole town on a new island by itself, in one of eight characters: harbour town, marble city, castle town, market town, river town, farming village, hill town or garden town.
- Towns save themselves in the browser and can be shared as a link or a picture postcard.
